chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Zareeh Al-Muharibi, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Whichever believer relieves a believer of a hardship, while he is insolvent, Allah will ease his needs in this world and the Hereafter.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And whoever covers a flaw of a believer that he fears, Allah will cover him with seventy flaws from the flaws of this world and the Hereafter.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'And Allah is aiding the believer as long as the believer is aiding his brother.'
So benefit yourselves with the advice and desire the goodness.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for relieving a believer's hardship and covering their flaws according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the reciprocal nature of divine assistance, linking the believer's effort to relieve another's distress with Allah's easing of their own needs in both worlds. The specific promise of covering 'seventy flaws' underscores the comprehensive mercy granted for concealing the faults of others, a key concept in Shia ethics of social harmony. It concludes with a practical exhortation to actively seek goodness and benefit from moral advice.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Jameel Bin Salih, from Zareeh Al Muhariby who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Whichever Momin relieves a suffering from a Momin and he is insolvent, Allahazwj would Ease his needs for him in the world and the Hereafter’.
Heasws said: ‘And the one who veils upon a Momin an exposure which he fears, Allahazwj would Veil seventy exposures from the exposures of the world and the Hereafter.
And Allahazwj Assists upon the Momin what the Momin was in assisting his brother,
therefore benefit yourselves with the advice and be desiring regarding the goodness’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Mahbub from Jamil ibn Salih from Dharih al-Muharibi who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘Any believer who relieves a believer from his hardships in a constraining condition Allah will make his (helper’s) needs easily met in this world and in the next.’

The Imam said, ‘Whoever provides cover for the private matters of a believer for which he is afraid, Allah will provide cover for his (helper’s) seventy private matters of this world and in the next life.’
The Imam said, ‘Allah supports a believer as long as he supports his believing brother (in belief).
You must benefit from the good advice and be interested in good deeds.’”
